2002:
** ἐπισωρ-εύω**,
**heap upon,** τινί τι {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 3.123e}}; **heap up, accumulate,** διδασκάλους {{NT+1st c.AD+|NT.2Tim.4.3; ἓν ἐξ ἑνός 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.10.5; ἀμηχανίας 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.830a}}:—_passive_, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|[prev. author] “in Hes.” 34, 2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 344.12.}}
2015:
** ἐπιφάν-εια**
(i.e. ἱερά), τά, **sacrifices in celebration of an** ἐπιφάνεια, Δημήτριος τὰ ἐ. τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ θύων {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Carystius Historicus 10.}}
2017:
** ἐπιφαύσκω**,
_future_ -φαύσω (see. below):— **shine out,** of the sun or moon, {{LXX|LXX.Job.25.5, 31.26}}: also in _passive_ form,{{Refs|[prev. work] 41.9(10)}}; ἐπιφαύσει σοι ὁ Χριστός **will shine out** for thee,{{NT|NT.Eph.5.14.}}
2023:
** ἐπιχορηγ-έω**,
**supply, furnish,** {{NT+2nd c.BC+|2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus “Dioptra” 31; σπέρμα τῷ σπείροντι NT.2Cor.9.10; ὑμῖν τὸ πνεῦμα NT.Gal.3.5; τὸ ἐοικέναι τοῖς νοητοῖς εἴδεσιν 5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 341}}; especially of a husband, **provide for** a wife, ἐ. τῇ γαμουμένῃ τὰ δέοντα {{Refs 1st c.AD+|“POxy.” 905.10 (2nd c.AD), compare 282.6 (1st c.AD)}}; conversely, ἐὰν [γυνὴ] ἐ. τῷ ἀνδρὶ αὐτῆς {{LXX|LXX.Sir.25.22(30)}}:—_passive_, τὰ ἀπὸ Λιμυρικῆς -ούμενα {{NT+1st c.BC+|“Periplus Maris Rubri [1st c.AD]” 60; τοῖς παρ᾽ ἑτέρων -ηθεῖσι πλούτοις 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.42; πᾶν τὸ σῶμα διὰ τῶν ἁφῶν..ἐπιχορηγούμενον καὶ συμβιβαζόμενον NT.Col.2.19.}}
2024:
** ἐπιχορηγ-ία**, ἡ,
**supply, provision,** τῆς ἐ. γενομένης ἐκ τῶν ἱερῶν προσόδων {{Refs 1st c.AD+|“SIG” 818.9 (Ephesus, 1st c.AD)}}; πᾶν τὸ σῶμα..συμβιβαζόμενον διὰ πάσης ἁφῆς τῆς ἐπιχορηγίας, ={διὰ πασῶν τῶν ἐπιχορηγουσῶν ἁφῶν} (compare ἐπιχορηγέω near the end), {{NT|NT.Eph.4.16; διὰ τῆς ἐ. τοῦ πνεύματος NT.Phil.1.19.}}
2034:
** ἑπτάκις** [ᾰ],
_adverb_ **seven times,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.40, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 698, etc.}}:— _poetry_ **ἑπτάκι** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 156, 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.861, etc.}}: also in later Prose, {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“SIG” 1068.8 (Patmos, 3rd-2nd c.BC), 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “in Nicomachi arithmeticam introductionem” p.17}} P.:—_Laconian dialect_ **ἑπτάκιν** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|“IG” 5(1).213.16 (5th c.BC).}}

** ἐραστ-ός**, ή, όν,
={ἐρατός}, **beloved, lovely,** in Prose the usual form, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Smp.” 204c, “Phdr.” 250d; also in [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus] 178.1; τόνδε δρόμον ποίησεν ἐραστόν “IG” 12.817}}: _comparative_, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|“AP” 12.197 (2nd c.AD: Strato Epigrammaticus).}}
2044:
** ἐρεύγομαι**,
**B** _aorist 2_ _active_ ἤρῠγον, **bellow, roar,** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|ἤρυγεν, ὡς ὅτε ταῦρος ἤρυγεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.403}}; τόν γ᾽ ἐρυγόντα λίπε..θυμός {{Refs|[prev. work] 406; ὅσον βαθὺς ἤρυγε λαιμός}} **roared** to the full depth of his throat or voice, {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 13.58}}; of the sea, ἀμφὶ δέ τ᾽ ἄκραι ἠϊόνες βοόωσιν ἐρευγομένης ἁλὸς ἔξω the headlands echo to the **roar** of the sea, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.265; κῦμα..δεινὸν ἐρευγόμενον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.403}}; ἐρεύγεται ἤπειρόνδε [{{LXX|[prev. work] 438 (compare βοάω 1.2):—so in later Gr., λέων ἐρεύξεται Vetus Testamentum Graece redditum LXX.Hos.11.10, LXX.Amos.3.8; σκύμνος ἐρευγόμενος LXX.1Mac.3.4; with variant{ὠρύομαι}, LXX.Eze.22.25; compare προσερεύγομαι. (Cf. Latin _rūgio_ 'roar'.)}}]
2050:
** ἐρήμ-ωσις**, εως, ἡ,
**making desolate,** {{LXX+2nd c.AD+|LXX.Lev.26.34, +others, 4th c.AD: Hephaestio Astrologus 1.21; χωρίου 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 1.9.7; βδέλυγμα τῶν ἐ. LXX.Dan.9.27, cf. NT.Matt.24.15.}}
2053:
** ἔριον**, τό,
_Ionic dialect_ **εἴριον** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|“GDI” iv (Chios, 4th c.BC, also written ἔρια [prev. passage]), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus, and always in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (indicating ἐρϝ-) except _genitive_ ἐρίοιο in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.124}}:— **wool,** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.434, Od.[same place], 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 175d}}; ἐρίῳ στέψαντες, i.e. with woollen fillets, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|[prev. author] “R.” 398a, etc.: frequently in _plural_, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.388, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.316}}; εἴρια ῥυπαρά, ἔρια οἰσυπηρά, greasy wool, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀγμῶν” 21, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 2.74; ἔρια καθαρά “PCair.Zen.” 12.62 (3rd c.BC)}}; τἄρια, crasis for τὰ ἔ., {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1387; οὖλα ἔρια [prev. work] 1067}}; ἔ. πεπταμένα outspread **flocks of wool,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|[prev. author] “Nu.” 343; ἐρίων τάλαντον [prev. author] “V.” 1147; τὰ Μιλήσια ἔ. 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 90.3, compare 4th c.BC: Amphis Comicus 27.1; εἴρια ἀπὸ ξύλου}}**cotton,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3. 47, compare 106}}; τὸ ἔ. [τῆς ἀράχνης] a spider's **web,** {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Philostrati majoris imagines” 2.28}}; τὰ ἐκ τῆς θαλάττης ἔ., of the **byssus** of the pinna, {{Refs 4th c.AD+|4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 1.2. (ἔρια “Schwyzer” 180 (from Crete) without initial ϝ-}}; Latin _vervex_ perhaps not _cognate_)

2057:
**Ἑρμᾶς**, -ᾶ, accusative, -ᾶν (Doric form of Ἑρμῆς),
**Hermas, a Christian**: Rom.16:14.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
2060: **Hermes **, the Lat. _Mercurius_, son of Maia and Zeus; messenger of the gods διάκτορος); giver of good luck ἐριούνιος, ἀκάκητα); god of all secret dealings, cunning, and stratagem δόλιος); bearing a golden rod χρυσόρραπις); conductor of defunct spirits ψυχοπομπός, πομπαῖος); tutelary god of all arts, of traffic, markets, roads ἀγοραῖος, ἐμπολαῖος, ὅδιος, ἐνόδιος); and of heralds. His bust, mounted on a four-cornered pillar, was used to mark boundaries. —;Proverb., κοινὸς Ἑρμῆς **shares in your luck! ** {{4th/3rd c.BC|Theophrastus Philosophus}}: compare ἕρμαιον. (Middle Liddel)

2094:
** ἔτος**, εος, τό,
irregular _dative_ ἔτῃ {{Refs|“IG” 2.1059.18}}:—**year**, τῶν προτέρων ἐτέων in bygone **years**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.691}}; τόδ᾽ ἐεικοστὸν ἔ. ἐστὶν ἐξ οὗ{{Refs 8th c.BC+|.. 24.765, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.89, 19.222; ὅτε.. ὄγδοόν μοι ἐπιπλόμενον ἔ. ἦλθε 7.261}}; ἔ. ἐνιαυτῶν, see at {ἐνιαυτό; ἑκάστου ἔτους} {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 58b; ἀν᾽ ἕκαστον ἔ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 4.4.4; ἀνὰ πᾶν ἔ. “Anthologia Graeca” 9.430 (1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Crinagoras Epigrammaticus); ἀνὰ πάντα ἔτεα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.65}}; δι᾽ ἔτους πέμπτου every fifth **year**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 584}}; κατὰ ἔ. every **year**, {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.53, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 3.2, NT.Luke.2.41, etc. (frequently καθ᾽ ἕ., as “PPetr.” 3p.34 (3rd c.BC) and later)}}; ἔ. εἰς ἔ. **year** after **year**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 340 (Lyric poetry)}}; δι᾽ ἔτους **annually**, {{LXX+3rd c.BC+|1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.19, 378; εἰς ἔ. 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus “Epigrammata” 13.4; εἰς ἔ. ἐξ ἔτεος [prev. author] 18.15; ἔ. ἐξ ἔτους LXX.Lev.25.50}}; παρὰ ἔ. every other **year**, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 9.32.3 (but πὰρ ϝέτος}}**yearly,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|Tab.Heracl. 1.101); πάλαι πολλὰ ἤδη ἔτη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 18b; τρίτῳ ἔτει 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.101; τρίτῳ ἔτεϊ πρότερον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.40}}; τρίτῳ ἔτεϊ τούτων in the third **year** after this, {{Refs|[prev. passage], etc.}}; frequently in _accusative_, ἔ. τόδ᾽ ἤδη δέκατον.. βόσκων now for these ten **years**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 312; τύραννος ἐγεγόνει ἤδη χιλιοστὸν ἔτος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 615c, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.4, 33.23}}; of a person's age, γεγονὼς ἔτη τρία ἀπολείποντα τῶν ἑκατόν {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.270; οἱ ὑπὲρ τὰ στρατεύσιμα ἔτη γεγονότες 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.4, compare 13, etc.}}; without γεγονώς, τοὺς ὑπὲρ τετταράκοντα ἔτη {{Refs|[prev. author] “An.” 5.3.1; οἱ μέχρι τετταράκοντα ἐτῶν [prev. work] 6.4.25}}, etc.: in _genitive_, ἐπειδὰν ἐτῶν ᾖ τις τριάκοντα {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 721b}}; μυρίων ἐτῶν **within a period** of {{Refs|10, 000}}**years**, [{{Refs|[prev. author] “Phdr.” 248e; ὥρα ἔτους, see at {ὥρα} 1.}}]
**2** **regnal year**, τὸ πέμπτον ἔ. Δομιτιανοῦ {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|“POxy.” 477.8 (2nd c.AD)}}. (**ϝέτος** {{Refs 6th c.BC+|“SIG” 9.2 (Olympia, 6th c.BC), “Berl.Sitzb.” 1927.8 (_Locrian dialect_, 5th c.BC), “Inscription Cyprian dialect” 135.1 H., “Tab.Heracl.”}}[same place]; cf. Latin _vetus._)
